title: CertMike
description: Author Mike Chapple’s site for security-certification study resources.

title: CompTIA Cybersecurity Analyst (CySA+) certification
description: Official CompTIA CySA+ certification page, including exam overview and objectives.

title: CompTIA certifications and exam vouchers
description: CompTIA’s current certifications hub, where exam vouchers are now purchased (the old store.comptia.org storefront redirects here).

title: Exploit Education
description: Free vulnerable VMs and challenges for learning exploit development; this is the official successor to exploit-exercises.com, which is no longer the real project site.

title: Hacking-Lab
description: Hands-on cyber security training platform with CTF-style exercises.

title: Pearson VUE CompTIA exam scheduling
description: Pearson VUE’s CompTIA testing page for scheduling in-person or online exams.

title: PentesterLab exercises
description: Web-app and pentest exercise catalog, including a subscription-based lab path.

title: CompTIA Continuing Education
description: How to keep a CompTIA certification current through the Continuing Education program.

title: CompTIA online (at-home) exam
description: CompTIA’s current write-up of the remotely proctored, at-home exam experience (the older testing-options URL now lands here).

title: Renew a CompTIA certification with a higher-level cert
description: CompTIA CE option for renewing a certification by earning a higher-level CompTIA cert.

title: Wiley Sybex online test bank
description: Online practice questions and test bank that come with the Sybex study guide.

title: Converting a VMware VMX file for VirtualBox
description: Walk-through for converting a VMware VM so it can run in VirtualBox.

title: Kali Linux downloads
description: Official Kali Linux download page, including virtual-machine images for the book’s labs. The older kali.org/downloads path now redirects here.

title: Metasploitable (SourceForge)
description: Intentionally vulnerable Metasploitable VM image, used in the book’s lab setup.

title: VMware OVF Tool
description: Official OVF Tool download (now on Broadcom’s developer site) for converting VM images, such as Metasploitable, for VirtualBox.

title: VirtualBox downloads
description: Free Type-2 hypervisor used in the book’s lab setup, with builds for Windows, macOS, and Linux.

title: NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1, Guide for Conducting Risk Assessments
description: NIST’s current publication page for the risk-assessment guide used in qualitative and quantitative risk discussions.

title: Docker
description: Official Docker site for container runtime and tooling used in containerized infrastructure.

title: Microsoft Azure: What is a container?
description: Microsoft overview of containerization concepts, complementary to the Docker discussion.

title: CIS Benchmarks
description: Center for Internet Security configuration benchmarks used as system-hardening baselines (the book also cited cisecurity.org/benchmark, which leads here).

title: CIS Microsoft Windows Desktop Benchmark
description: CIS hardening benchmark for Windows desktop releases, including the Windows 11 stand-alone guide used in a chapter 2 lab.

title: Protecting Linux configuration files
description: Article on practices for protecting Linux configuration files (encryption, access control, and related controls).

title: The Defender's Guide to the Windows Registry
description: Defender-oriented walkthrough of how the Windows Registry is structured and how to monitor it for abuse.

title: Windows system processes: an overview for blue teams
description: Blue-team reference listing legitimate Windows system processes, paths, and parent/child relationships.

title: How to install and configure NTP on Linux
description: Distribution-agnostic guide to installing and configuring NTP on Linux systems.

title: Windows Time Service tools and settings
description: Microsoft documentation for configuring and troubleshooting Windows time synchronization, which is critical for log correlation.

title: Shared Assessments
description: Industry tools and questionnaires for assessing the security of cloud and other third-party providers. The public site presented a sign-in interstitial when checked.

title: FBI Major Case 216 (NCDIR) case study
description: FBI/NCSA case study of a long-running intrusion set, used in the book to illustrate federated-identity and access-monitoring issues. The original Illinois blog PDF is gone; this is the same report in the university’s IDEALS repository.

title: OWASP SAML Security Cheat Sheet
description: OWASP guidance on common SAML implementation flaws and how to harden federated single sign-on.

title: Microsoft AD FS overview (legacy)
description: Archived Microsoft overview of Active Directory Federation Services, now hosted on Microsoft Learn.

title: BeyondTrust: Privileged Access Management (PAM)
description: Vendor glossary article explaining privileged access management concepts and life-cycle control of privileged accounts.

title: Symmetric vs. asymmetric encryption (video)
description: Short video explainer of symmetric and asymmetric encryption, used as a PKI primer in the book.

title: Metasploitable (Rapid7)
description: Rapid7’s current Metasploitable information and download page for the intentionally vulnerable lab VM.

title: VMware Workstation and Fusion
description: Current VMware desktop hypervisor page (Workstation/Fusion replaced the old Workstation Player product page).

title: Simulating a beacon
description: Active Countermeasures techniques for generating beacon-like traffic so you can test whether your network defenses would catch it.

title: MAC Vendor Lookup
description: Lookup tool that maps a MAC address prefix to a hardware vendor during network investigations.

title: MAC Vendors
description: Another MAC-address OUI lookup service for identifying device manufacturers.

title: NIST National Software Reference Library (NSRL)
description: NIST library of known software hashes used to filter known-good files during investigations and forensic triage.

title: Wazuh
description: Open-source security platform with file-integrity monitoring, log analysis, and host detection capabilities.

title: Microsoft Sysinternals
description: Microsoft Sysinternals suite and documentation. The book also mentions running individual tools live from https://live.sysinternals.com/.

title: SANS Hunt Evil poster
description: Current SANS DFIR “Hunt Evil” poster (successor to the 2014 “Know Normal… Find Evil” PDF) summarizing normal vs. suspicious Windows artifacts.

title: Getting started with Windows debugging
description: Microsoft Learn guide to WinDbg and Windows debugging, which the book points to for crash-dump analysis (the old MSDN article redirects here).

title: OWASP Top 10
description: OWASP’s flagship list of the most critical web application security risks, often used as a default WAF ruleset baseline.

title: Daniel Miessler: tcpdump walkthrough
description: Practical introduction to capturing and filtering packets with tcpdump.

title: HackerTarget: tcpdump examples
description: Collection of ready-to-use tcpdump command examples for common investigation tasks.

title: Whois.com
description: Web WHOIS lookup service; the book notes that “whois” is a general technique as well as this specific site.

title: DNSChecker email header analyzer
description: Online analyzer that breaks down received-from chains, authentication results, and other header details.

title: Mailfence: email header guide
description: Plain-language explanation of email header fields and how to read them during phishing analysis.

title: Understanding an email header (Media Temple)
description: The book’s email-header primer; the old Media Temple article now redirects to a generic GoDaddy offer page, so use the Mailfence or MXToolbox links instead.

title: WhatIsMyIP email header analyzer
description: Web tool that parses raw email headers into a more readable investigation view.

title: DMARC overview
description: Official overview of DMARC and how it builds on SPF and DKIM to authenticate mail.

title: Sender Policy Framework (SPF) explained
description: Current Mimecast explainer for SPF (the book’s dmarcanalyzer.com/spf page now redirects here after the Mimecast acquisition).

title: Cuckoo Sandbox
description: Open-source malware sandbox; cuckoosandbox.org failed a connectivity check, so this points at the widely used CERT-EE public Cuckoo instance. The project code is also at https://github.com/cuckoosandbox/cuckoo.

title: Joe Sandbox
description: Commercial (with a free tier) multi-OS malware sandbox named in the exam outline.

title: VirusTotal
description: Multi-engine malware and URL scanning service, useful for checking suspicious files and hashes.

title: Regular-Expressions.info quick start
description: Short regex primer; enough background for the exam’s pattern-matching expectations without becoming a regex expert.

title: MXToolbox Email Headers
description: Email-header analysis tool used in the chapter 3 lab to decode phishing-message headers.

title: Zeltser: looking up malicious websites
description: Lenny Zeltser’s list of reputation and lookup tools for checking suspicious URLs and domains from phishing emails.

title: AlienVault Open Threat Exchange (OTX)
description: Community threat-intelligence platform (also cited via cybersecurity.att.com/open-threat-exchange) for browsing pulses, IoCs, and reputation data; used in a chapter 4 lab.

title: CISA Automated Indicator Sharing (AIS)
description: CISA program for automated, machine-to-machine sharing of cyber threat indicators.

title: CISA Information Sharing and Analysis Organizations (ISAOs)
description: CISA page on ISAOs, the broader information-sharing communities beyond formal ISACs.

title: CISA cybersecurity alerts and advisories
description: Current CISA alerts and advisories feed; the former US-CERT site now redirects to the CISA homepage, so this is the useful replacement.

title: Cisco Security Center
description: Cisco’s security research and advisory portal (the older tools.cisco.com URL now lands here).

title: Cisco Talos Intelligence
description: Cisco Talos threat research site and reputation-lookup tools.

title: Department of Defense Cyber Crime Center (DC3)
description: U.S. DoD Cyber Crime Center, a government source of cybercrime and threat information.

title: MISP threat-sharing feeds
description: MISP project feed listings for community-shared, standardized threat intelligence.

title: Microsoft threat intelligence blog
description: Microsoft Security blog posts tagged for threat intelligence and actor research.

title: Senki open-source threat intelligence feeds
description: Curated list of open-source threat-intelligence feeds and related operator tooling.

title: ThreatFeeds.io
description: Directory of open-source threat-intelligence feeds with metadata about maintainers and update cadence.

title: Australian Cyber Security Centre
description: Australian Signals Directorate Cyber Security Centre, an example of a national government cyber-threat site.

title: SANS Internet Storm Center
description: SANS ISC daily threat diaries, handler notes, and community observations of emerging internet attacks.

title: Spamhaus
description: Block lists and reputation data for spam, hijacked networks, and networks you may not want to peer with (SBL, XBL, PBL, DROP).

title: VirusShare
description: Large malware-sample repository used by researchers (access is typically request-based).

title: Tor Browser download
description: Official Tor Browser download, needed if you are exploring dark-web sites that are only reachable over Tor.

title: ThreatConnect confidence / “skulls” scale
description: The book’s example of a six-level threat-confidence scale. ThreatConnect was acquired by Dataminr and this specific article no longer resolves to the original resource.

title: OASIS CTI documentation (STIX and TAXII)
description: Official documentation for STIX (Structured Threat Information Expression) and the TAXII transport protocol.

title: National Council of ISACs
description: Umbrella organization for U.S. sector-based Information Sharing and Analysis Centers.

title: CISA critical infrastructure sectors
description: Official list and descriptions of U.S. critical-infrastructure sectors and their sector-specific partners.

title: UK National Protective Security Authority (NPSA)
description: UK national protective-security authority; this is the successor to the Centre for the Protection of National Infrastructure (CPNI). The site returned a block/unavailable page from this checker.

title: The Honeynet Project
description: Open-source honeypot and honeynet projects used to collect attacker techniques for active defense and research.

title: Anomali STAXX
description: Anomali’s STAXX community threat-intelligence platform, which the chapter 4 lab asks you to install. The current product page still advertises a download; confirm availability before relying on it for a lab, and consider OTX or MISP as alternatives.

title: Anomali STAXX installation guide (PDF)
description: STAXX installation and administration PDF cited in the book’s lab. The host failed a TLS handshake from this checker, so the guide may no longer be published at this URL.

title: ISECOM research (OSSTMM)
description: Institute for Security and Open Methodologies research page, home of the Open Source Security Testing Methodology Manual.

title: NIST SP 800-115, Technical Guide to Information Security Testing and Assessment
description: NIST’s official page (and PDF) for security testing and assessment methodology, including reconnaissance and evaluation techniques.

title: Penetration Testing Execution Standard (PTES)
description: Community pentest methodology standard cited alongside OSSTMM and NIST SP 800-115. The site did not complete a TLS handshake from this checker and may be offline.

title: hping source and documentation
description: Source and docs for the hping packet-crafting tool. The old wiki.hping.org site no longer presents a working TLS service; this GitHub repo is the project’s current home.

title: Metasploit Unleashed
description: OffSec’s free Metasploit Unleashed course, covering modules, scanning, and exploitation workflows.

title: Metasploit documentation
description: Official Metasploit Framework documentation, including scanning and auxiliary modules mentioned in the book.

title: Identifying incidents via syslog (Cisco)
description: Cisco guidance on using syslog from network devices to spot security incidents.

title: BGP looking glasses
description: List of public BGP looking-glass servers for inspecting how a target’s networks are routed on the internet.

title: Sanmay Ved: I purchased the domain Google.com
description: First-person account of a Google Domains registration glitch, used in the book to illustrate domain-ownership and reconnaissance surprises.

title: DigiNinja Zone Transfer Me
description: Practice DNS zone you are allowed to AXFR against, for learning zone-transfer reconnaissance.

title: DomainTools WHOIS history
description: Historical WHOIS research service for seeing how a domain’s registration has changed over time.

title: NIST Security Content Automation Protocol (SCAP)
description: NIST project page for SCAP, including related standards such as OVAL used in automated vulnerability assessment.

title: Nessus Essentials
description: Free Nessus Essentials activation and product page for lab and small-scale scanning.

title: Nessus downloads
description: Tenable’s Nessus scanner download page, used in the chapter 6 lab.

title: Tenable Nessus documentation
description: Official Nessus documentation for installation, scanning, and report review.

title: NVD CVSS v3 calculator
description: NIST’s interactive CVSS v3 calculator for scoring vulnerabilities the way the book and many scan reports still present them.

title: FIRST CVSS specification
description: Official CVSS specification. The same URL now serves CVSS v4.0; the book’s examples are CVSS v3, which FIRST still documents alongside the current version.

title: Verizon Data Breach Investigations Report (DBIR)
description: Annual Verizon DBIR, cited for real-world breach and vulnerability-exploitation trends.

title: Microsoft product life-cycle information
description: Microsoft product life-cycle search, for tracking end-of-support dates that drive patch and upgrade decisions.

title: Dirty COW (CVE-2016-5195)
description: Researchers’ site for the Dirty COW Linux privilege-escalation vulnerability, with background and patching guidance.

title: OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet
description: OWASP recommendations for robust session handling to reduce impersonation and session-attack risk.

title: Cisco Talos Reputation Center
description: Talos reputation-lookup console for IPs, domains, and related threat-reputation research.

title: OWASP static code analysis
description: OWASP wiki page listing static-analysis concepts and tools (including OWASP’s own analyzers).

title: UC Berkeley Minimum Security Standards for Electronic Information
description: Example of a university security standard that maps required controls to data-protection levels.

title: Visa: What to Do If Compromised
description: Visa’s mandatory merchant procedure for responding to a suspected payment-card compromise, used as an example of a required procedure.

title: Washington state electronic signature guidelines
description: State of Washington guidelines on electronic signatures, used in the book as an example of non-mandatory guidance (now hosted by WaTech).

title: National Archives General Records Schedule 3.2
description: U.S. federal records schedule that, among other things, requires incident-handling records to be retained for at least three years (Item 20).

title: Cortex XSOAR ransomware playbook
description: Public Cortex XSOAR ransomware-response playbook, cited as an example of a structured incident playbook.

title: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2, Computer Security Incident Handling Guide
description: NIST’s official page for the incident-handling guide used throughout the book (PDF still available). Rev. 3 is in draft at https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/61/r3/ipd as a CSF 2.0 community profile.

title: UCF Windows incident response playbook
description: University of Central Florida procedure for Windows incident response, cited as a real-world playbook example.

title: MITRE ATT&CK
description: MITRE ATT&CK knowledge base of adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures used for threat modeling and detection engineering.

title: The Diamond Model of Intrusion Analysis
description: Caltagirone, Pendergast, and Betz’s Diamond Model paper (adversary, infrastructure, capability, victim). The original DTIC PDF URL now lands on a maintenance page; this is a widely used public copy of the same report.

title: Lockheed Martin Cyber Kill Chain
description: Lockheed Martin’s Cyber Kill Chain paper, covering the reconnaissance-through-actions-on-objectives sequence used in the exam.

title: The Unified Kill Chain
description: Unified Kill Chain paper that combines the Cyber Kill Chain, ATT&CK, and other models into a single end-to-end sequence (useful background, not a named exam objective).

title: OSSTMM (Open Source Security Testing Methodology Manual)
description: Direct PDF of OSSTMM version 3, a testing methodology the exam expects you to recognize.

title: OWASP Web Security Testing Guide
description: OWASP’s testing guide for web application security assessments, listed among exam-relevant testing resources.

title: SANS Holiday Hack Challenges
description: Free annual SANS holiday CTF challenges, useful practice for IoCs and incident-response puzzles.

title: PostgreSQL monitoring wiki
description: PostgreSQL wiki page listing monitoring tools and approaches, used when discussing database resource-usage IoCs.

title: OSSEC downloads
description: Open Source HIDS (OSSEC) download page; a host-based integrity and log-monitoring tool cited for file-change IoCs.

title: Cloudflare: DNS amplification DDoS
description: Explainer of DNS amplification attacks, in which small queries to open resolvers generate large responses toward a victim.

title: Cloudflare: fast-flux DNS
description: Explainer of fast-flux (and double fast-flux) DNS, a technique malware operators use to rapidly rotate infrastructure.

title: Elastic Security Analytics Recipes
description: Example Elasticsearch machine-learning recipes, including one for spotting suspicious login activity.

title: PwC summary of U.S. cyber breach-reporting legislation
description: PwC overview of cyber breach-reporting requirements, including CIRCIA’s incident and ransomware-payment reporting timelines.

title: CISA CRR Resource Guide: Incident Management
description: CISA Cyber Resilience Review resource guide for incident management, including an example incident-report template.

title: LastPass notice of 2022 security incident
description: LastPass public notification of its 2022 security incident, used as a sample incident report. The post was updated to this canonical path; the blog blocked automated requests from this checker.

title: Microsoft DEV-0537 (LAPSUS$) intrusion report
description: Public Microsoft incident write-up on the DEV-0537/LAPSUS$ actor, used as a chapter 12 reporting-and-communication example.

title: NISTIR 8006, Cloud Computing Forensic Science Challenges
description: Final (2020) NIST report on cloud-forensics challenges; the book cited an earlier draft PDF.

title: NIST Computer Forensics Tool Testing (CFTT)
description: NIST CFTT program page, including hardware write-blocker testing that the book referenced for evidence preservation.

title: NIST CFReDS Data Leakage Case
description: NIST forensic practice image of an intellectual-property-theft scenario, used for the chapter 13 worked example.

title: Forensics Wiki
description: Community digital-forensics wiki (the book notes that forensicswiki.org moved here). Content is also maintained on GitHub at https://github.com/forensicswiki/wiki.

title: Forensics Wiki source (GitHub)
description: GitHub source repository for the Forensics Wiki, useful if the public wiki is down or you want to browse the raw pages.

title: Stroz Friedberg forensic report (Ceglia / Facebook case)
description: Public forensic report from the Ceglia v. Facebook case, used to discuss lessons learned and older forensic artifacts. The original Wired PDF is gone; this is a widely mirrored copy of the same Stroz Friedberg report (also in the court record).

title: NIST CFReDS forensic images
description: Archive of NIST Computer Forensic Reference Data Sets, including the Rhino Hunt practice image used in the chapter 13 lab. A newer CFReDS portal is advertised at cfreds.nist.gov, but that host failed a TLS check from here.

title: SANS SIFT Workstation
description: Free SANS forensic and incident-response VM (SIFT), which the book uses with the NIST Rhino Hunt exercise.

title: Nmap OS detection methods
description: Nmap reference on the probes and tests used for operating-system fingerprinting, cited in the chapter 6 answer key.
